title: CEL evaluator lacks window/consecutive support for Four in a Row
description: The built-in CEL evaluator (cel.py) supports exists/all/filter on lists but has no integer indexing or window/slice operation. The four_in_a_row win condition requires checking 4 consecutive same-owner cells in any direction on a 7x6 board. The current rows/cols/lines variables contain full rows (length 7) and full cols (length 6); a .all() check would require ALL cells to be owned, not just 4. Options: (1) add integer indexing to _parse_postfix so window-iteration is expressible in CEL, (2) precompute all 4-cell windows as a lines_4 variable in _populate_grid_lines, (3) support WASM for game-specific win logic. Until resolved, four_in_a_row.json uses a placeholder condition and tests verify placement only.
close_reason: Added lines_N windowed sub-lines to both Python and Rust CEL contexts. Updated four-in-a-row.json to use lines_4.exists(). All win/draw tests now verify engine end conditions.
